name: Mangrove folk
one_line: They built the town on legs over the tide and kept the fish alive in a walled pond; the streets were water, the wealth was honey, and the shells piled up into an island.

needs: tidal forest at the site: roots the tide covers and uncovers, a channel a boat can use at low water
a fresh seep or river arm to drink from; nipa marks it

staples: oysters and cockles off the stilt roots
fish and shrimp from the fence and the pond
nipa sugar and the sour fruit of the mangrove apple
how: a fence of stakes and screens across a tidal creek; the ebb leaves the fish behind it; basket traps in the channels
oysters cut from the roots at low tide, from the boat
a hook on a line under the roots for the mud crab; a spear from the boat over the shallows
the pond: fry come in on the spring tide and are kept until wanted
smoke a wild hive deep in the forest, in season
preserve: smoking over a slow fire on the platform; shrimp sun-dried on the walkway
nipa vinegar to keep fish; honey keeps itself

fuel.note: mangrove wood is dense and burns hot and slow, the long-night log; dry fronds for the quick fire; green leaves for the honey smoke; a kiln of it makes the best charcoal there is, a craft the ruins ran

shelter.form: houses on poles above the highest tide, a hearth box of clay on the floor, walkways of poles between them, boats moored underneath; a family without a house lives in its boat

MANGROVE.fuel: mangrove log and branch; frond for the quick fire
MANGROVE.food: crab, oysters off the roots, pond fish, honey in season
MANGROVE.shelter: poles over the tide, nipa thatch, walkways between
MANGROVE.palette: root red, mud, green over tannin-brown water

ESTUARY.fuel: branch, driftwood the river brings, reeds
ESTUARY.food: mullet and shrimp in the fence, cockles, the thickest nipa: sugar and vinegar
ESTUARY.shelter: stilt houses strung along the channel bank
ESTUARY.palette: silt brown, nipa green, brown water

LAGOON.food: reef fish speared from the boat, sea-grass shellfish, crab
LAGOON.shelter: houses far out over the shallows, boats under the floors

knows: nipa palm: sewn thatch; the flower stalk tapped for sap, boiled to sugar or soured to vinegar; the young fruit
sea purslane and saltwort as greens
mangrove fern shoots to eat; the fern stands where the water is fresh
mangrove apple fruit, sour and safe; which flowering tells you the hives are full
mangrove bark to tan lines and nets so they do not rot
plantkeeper.teaches_flavour: why the honey tastes of the forest: the bees work whichever mangrove is in flower; why the midden grows plants the mud does not
plantkeeper.teaches_practical: greens against the months of fish and salt; the fern means fresh water; vinegar keeps a catch the smoke cannot

makes: the stilt house and its walkway
wants_from_player: a blade: obsidian, or bog iron from the marsh smith

techniques.name: Fishpond
techniques.verb: wall a pond in the back-basin of the forest with mud bunds and a gate of poles; fry come in on the spring tide and fatten on the green scum until wanted
techniques.teaches: fish kept alive is storage without salt or smoke, the hinge of the ladder; the headman teaches it because it is how this land feeds a village, and because a pond walled small is the difference between a village and a drowned forest
techniques.unlocks: the camp's fish_run ceiling; a camp on a ruin's bunds has it the first season

techniques.name: Stilt house
techniques.verb: drive mangrove poles into the mud, lash a platform above the highest tide, thatch it with nipa; a hearth box of clay on the floor; boats for streets
techniques.teaches: the water is not the house's enemy but its road; a house that floods was built low
techniques.unlocks: a house over the water; the camp's shelter and its walkways

techniques.name: Honey
techniques.verb: in the flowering season go deep by boat, find the rock-bee comb hung under a bough, smoke it with a torch of green leaves, cut the honey side and leave the brood
techniques.teaches: the sweetest thing in the world, taken from the most dangerous place in it; half the comb is left so the hive comes back, restraint you can taste
techniques.unlocks: honey and wax: the mangrove's trade good up the river

techniques.name: Oysters off the roots
techniques.verb: at low tide, from the boat, cut the oysters off the stilt roots with a knife: the oyster, never the root
techniques.teaches: the roots are the oyster's bed and the fish's nursery; cut the root and the bed is gone in a year
techniques.unlocks: the player gathers oysters and cockles at low tide in any tidal forest

techniques.name: Forest garden
techniques.verb: plant useful trees wherever you camp: nipa at the fresh fringe, coconut on the bank, candlenut behind the houses
techniques.teaches: roof, light and sweet grow at the door if someone planted them; a ruin is found by its grove
techniques.unlocks: the camp's shelter and light ceilings: nipa thatch that sheds a monsoon, nipa sugar and vinegar, candlenuts; the nipa stand at a ruin is its signpost

techniques.name: Candlenuts
techniques.verb: string the oil-rich nuts on a palm-leaf rib and light the end; they burn one after another
techniques.teaches: each nut burns about a quarter of an hour, so the rib is a clock as well as a light
techniques.unlocks: a short tropical light the player carries; the nuts come from the grove behind the camp

gives: mangrove poles and shell for lime
wants: salt (no sun for pans under the rain)
a blade of obsidian or bog iron

ladder: fire in a clay box on a platform over the tide
the fish fence, then the pond: the fish_run
smoke racks, the vinegar jar, the sugar pot; the midden begins
honey and wax go up the river in the dugout
growth.restraint: poles cut from the landward stand, the seaward fringe left to breed the fish; the pond walled small in the back-basin, never the whole forest; the oyster cut off the root, never the root off the tree; half the comb left, and the hives only in season
growth.ceiling_hint: a river mouth with nipa at the fringe, a pond in the basin and hives in the back forest reaches the tribal ceiling; a thin fringe on a rock coast stays a family and a boat

signatures.what: rows of stumps in the mud, seen at low tide, where houses stood on poles
signatures.restore: restored: new poles go in beside the old stubs
signatures.inherits: the line of the old town; the first house goes up in a season

signatures.what: a mound of oyster and cockle shell rising out of the tidal forest, white under the roots; lime-rich, so different plants grow on it
signatures.restore: cleared: the new camp's shell goes on the old heap
signatures.inherits: dry ground above the tide, and the site's proof that it fed people

signatures.what: low mud walls in rectangles through the forest, mangrove grown back along them, water still standing inside at low tide
signatures.restore: restored: the wall patched and a gate hung; the pond fills on the next spring tide
signatures.inherits: the fishpond from the first season

signatures.what: a cut in the bank with a ramp of logs and packed shell, a hollow where boats were dragged up
a low round mound of burnt clay and black earth at the forest edge, charcoal crumbs in it, nothing growing on it
signatures.inherits: a floor baked hard; proof the old people burned charcoal here, a rung above the camp

ruin.plants_differ: the midden grows lime-lovers above the tide (buttonwood, sea purslane thickets, a strangler fig) where the forest around is root and mud; nipa stands mark where people planted it at a freshwater seep

aesthetic.silhouette: houses on legs over the water, walkways of poles between them, boats moored under the floors, smoke through thatch
sounds: fiddler crabs clicking on the mud
a paddle, then bees in the flowering trees
props: a dugout pulled up on the landing
fish traps drying on the walkway
the pond gate and a smoke torch of green leaves

real_world.analogue: Sundarbans honey collectors (mawali / mouli) and Bonbibi
real_world.note: rock bees (Apis dorsata) hang their combs in the mangrove; the mouli go in by boat in the spring flowering season, invoke Bonbibi, the forest's guardian honoured by Hindus and Muslims alike, against the tiger, and smoke and cut the comb; tigers take collectors every year

brackish ponds banked off in the mangrove for milkfish fry the tide brings; a Javanese law of 1400 CE already punished 'him who steals from a tambak', and ponds were likely on Mactan before 1521; ponds made too many ate the mangroves in the 20th century, the restraint rule in the record

lived on lepa houseboats (a dugout keel built up with strakes, a house amidships) and in stilt villages over the reef shallows; free-diving spearfishers and esteemed boat-builders; most have since moved to land

women cut the West African mangrove oyster off the stilt roots at low tide and cook and smoke it; since 2007 some 500 harvesters in 15 villages keep an eight-month closed season and use knives that spare the root

218 shell mounds, some hundreds of metres long, built over about two thousand years of cockle and oyster gathering; 28 are burial tumuli, baobabs grow on them, and the delta's villages still live by shellfish and fishing
Rhizophora cut for charcoal and poles on a 30-year rotation under management since 1902, the kilns in the forest; the nearest thing to a mangrove coppice

real_world.region: estuaries of Southeast Asia, India to Australia
real_world.note: roofs of sewn nipa thatch; the flower stalk tapped for sweet sap about thirty days a stalk, boiled to sugar or left to sour into vinegar or tuba; spreads by floating seed and by planting

real_world.region: Pacific mangrove coast of Colombia and Ecuador, c. 350 BCE-400 CE
real_world.note: houses on piles in the tidal forest, earthen mounds (tolas), raised fields whose channels held water and drew fish; the first people known to work platinum
